title: Blockchain
summary: Shared, cryptographically verifiable systems for recording and agreeing on state changes across a network.

title: Cryptocurrency
summary: Digital assets whose ownership and transfer are recorded through blockchain or related distributed systems.

title: Wallets & Security
summary: Key management, signing, custody, permissions, transaction review, phishing defense, and wallet safety.

title: Smart Contracts
summary: Programs deployed to blockchain-compatible execution environments that manage state, permissions, assets, and application logic.

title: DeFi
summary: Blockchain-based financial protocols for exchange, lending, liquidity, collateral, stablecoins, and programmable financial services.

title: Web3
summary: Applications and infrastructure built around cryptographic ownership, open protocols, blockchain systems, and programmable digital assets.

title: Blockchain Infrastructure
summary: Nodes, RPC services, validators, execution environments, indexing, bridges, interoperability, and operational blockchain systems.

title: Enterprise Blockchain
summary: Business deployment requirements including predictability, governance, integration, privacy, security, compliance, and operational reliability.

title: AI + Blockchain
summary: The intersection of AI agents, machine identity, programmable payments, permissions, verifiable records, and autonomous infrastructure.

definition: A shared data system in which network participants maintain and validate an ordered history of state changes.
A structured collection of transactions or state transitions accepted into a blockchain's history.
A signed request or recorded action that changes or references blockchain state.
A computer or service that participates in a blockchain network by maintaining, validating, or relaying network data.
The process or protocol through which network participants agree on valid state.
The point at which a blockchain transaction or state transition is considered sufficiently irreversible under the network's rules.
A digitally represented asset whose ownership and transfer are recorded through a blockchain or related distributed system.
A digital asset created through application or smart-contract logic on top of an existing blockchain network.
An asset built into a blockchain protocol and commonly used for network fees, staking, or economic coordination.
A digital asset designed to track or maintain a relatively stable reference value through a specified mechanism.
Software or hardware that helps a user manage keys, addresses, and transaction signing.
A public identifier associated with a blockchain account or transaction destination.
Secret cryptographic material used to authorize signatures and blockchain actions.
A human-readable recovery representation used by many wallet systems to derive or restore cryptographic keys.
Cryptographic proof that an authorized key approved a message or transaction.
Program logic deployed to a blockchain-compatible execution environment.
A unit or mechanism used by some blockchain execution environments to meter computational work or transaction resource usage.
The current set of data values a blockchain network recognizes at a given point in its execution history.
Blockchain-based financial applications implemented through smart contracts and digital assets.
A protocol or application that enables asset exchange through blockchain-based execution rather than a traditional centralized order custodian.
The availability of assets or counterparties that allows transactions to occur with limited price impact.
Assets pledged or locked to secure an obligation such as a blockchain-based loan.
A broad term for internet applications and infrastructure that use blockchain, cryptographic ownership, decentralized systems, and programmable assets.
An application that uses blockchain or decentralized infrastructure for some part of its state, execution, ownership, or coordination.
A remote procedure call interface used by applications and services to query or submit requests to blockchain nodes.
A network participant responsible for validating, proposing, attesting to, or otherwise helping finalize blockchain state under a consensus protocol.
The ability of different networks, protocols, or applications to exchange data, assets, or messages.
The processes and rules used to make decisions about a blockchain network, protocol, application, or shared resource.
Software that uses artificial intelligence to interpret goals, make decisions, and perform actions through tools or connected systems.
